subject: Geopolitics
title: Battery Recycling Wars
description: A fast breakdown of Battery Recycling Wars for builders.

hook.text: By 2030, 11 million tons of spent EV batteries will pile up. The minerals inside are too valuable to waste.

buildup.text: Battery recycling recovers lithium, cobalt, and nickel. It's cheaper and cleaner than mining new material.

discovery.text: Nations that master recycling reduce dependence on foreign mines. Urban mining on old batteries is the next frontier.

twist.text: China already recycles more batteries than anyone. It's building a closed loop that locks in supply advantage.

climax.text: The EU mandated recycled content in new batteries by 2031. Legislation is forcing the industry to close the loop.

punchline.text: Tomorrow's mine is today's recycling bin.

quiz.question: Why is battery recycling becoming geopolitically important?
options: Recycled batteries are faster to charge
It reduces dependence on foreign mineral mines
Batteries can only be used once before disposal
